newsitem.title: UK: LME copper prices edge back after hectic day.
newsitem.headline: LME copper prices edge back after hectic day.

text.p: Copper prices edged back from their kerb close and the 2-1/2 month high struck earlier by 1900 GMT on Friday.

By then the London Metal Exchange's (LME) flag ship contract was trading at $2,140/$2,145, about $12 off the day's high and $8 down from the kerb close following a gain based on declining warehouse inventories and widening backwardations.
A rise of over five percent was seen during a dramataic day featuring waves of fund buying, shortcovering and option delta purchases, traders said.
"Copper was the only game in town today - the others hardly moved in comparison. Everybody is a bit shell-shocked now," one trader said.
There was barely any movement in the other metals during the evening session with all the contracts remaining within their kerb close buy-sell spreads.
